It could be implemented like this:
- When no tool call skills are defined by the user the system works as is so that existing configurations work as before
- When tool call skills exists in either ~/.config/opencode/skills or project /.opencode/skills tool call descriptions won't be loaded in system prompt but just the short skill descriptions
- Add an option to fully load the skill tool calls instructions into the system prompt so that models that struggle with skills work the same as before, but with the option to fine tune the tool calling and add new tool calls. 
- Option to export tool call descriptions as skills into project folder ie opencode --export-toolcalls <path>. With "opencode --export-toolcalls ." it'll be exported to the project .opencode/skills. No path will export to the global opencode config, or use --global explicitly. Something like that.
- Check if existing skills interfere with opencode tool call skills before exporting. A --force overwrites them for example. Could add a rename existing skill, but that could be confusing.
- The models .json file could contain sensible defaults. ie if some models are known to struggle with skill tool calls, default would be to always load them fully into system prompt. LLMs that don't really need tool call instructions could default to no skill descriptions at all, if that will ever happen. 
- One could consider tool call instructions with different verbosity levels so that LLMs that struggle get the full clear description with examples and more capable models can do with more short, concise and succinct instructions without examples. Just like there are different agent prompts for Anthropic, Codex, Qwen with varying degrees of verbosity etc.

Thoughts?

> only stable solution I had so far is rewriting/normalizing paths to forward slashes

I don't follow. do you do it via some sort of hooks prior to executing each command?

> Does this also allow an `Agent` that calls a sub-agent via `Task` to pass a variant? One of the use cases I see is that the default model is not set (because I often switch between Providers) but you have e.g. Opus or Sonnet do the planning with maximum thinking but the `Agent` that will receive the sub-tasks should not have thinking enabled at all (or lower).

@terwey Quick check - if your goal is simply "Main agent currently running in High mode, worker **always** runs in Low mode", this PR (and mine #7156) already handles that via a frontmatter config. You can just set `variant: "low"` in your worker agent's file, and it will respect that setting even if the Main agent is running in "High" mode (subagents don't inherit parent variant).

However, since you mentioned "duplicating agents" as a workaround, I assume you need the flexibility to call the *same* worker agent sometimes with Low variant and sometimes with High (or changing models dynamically).

For that dynamic workflow, we could add new `model` and `variant` parameters to the `Task` tool schema so you can explicitly override it at call time:
`Thinking: "Calling worker agent with Claude 4.5 Haiku set to low variant..."`
`Call: /task agent=worker model=anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 variant=low`

**The Trade-offs:**
I feel like an agent is often a "bundle" of `{System Prompt + Model}`. I'd love your (and @rekram1-node's) thoughts on the risks of breaking that bundle dynamically? I had Gemini generate some examples:
1.  **Prompt Incompatibility**:
    *   **Scenario**: An oracle agent uses Claude 4.5 and its system prompt relies on `<userStyle/>` tags or other specific XML structures.
    *   **Failure**: A user overrides with `model="glm-4.7-free"` because their Claude plan is rate-limited. The model treats the XML tags as literal text, possibly degrading output quality without throwing an error. The "Oracle" may become a confused GLM-4.7 instance.
2.  **Context Window Overflows**:
    *   **Scenario**: A bug-investigator agent is designed for `gemini-3-pro` (2M context) and is passed a large log file.
    *   **Failure**: Caller overrides to `gpt-5.2` (128k context) thinking that it's a smarter model. The task fails immediately or, worse, silently truncates context, leading to incorrect answers.
3.  **Cost/Safety Bypass**:
    *   **Scenario**: A shell-caller agent is configured to use `claude-4-5-haiku` to keep costs low for background tasks.
    *   **Failure**: The user (or the main LLM agent) accidentally overrides it to `o3-pro`. The user would then lose architectural control over cost and latency.

Is explicit override what we want here (accepting those risks)? Or do we feel like they're overblown? If so, I'm happy to add the override parameters to my PR #7156 if we agree the flexibility outweighs the risk!

The exact point is that I don't want to have multiple agents preconfigured tied to a provider or thinking. This might be great for defaults, but right now I need to _restart_ opencode when I run out of tokens for a specific model.

I right now "solved" (but still tied to a provider) by having an agent `implementer` without a model and `implementer-fast` fixed to sonnet-no-thinking. This works, however I sometimes want a middle ground and not burn my tokens for Opus because something was slightly more complicated than fast could handle.

Ideally, this feature would be intelligent enough to disable auto-scroll only when the user has intentionally scrolled up from the bottom of the window. This is how many other LLM chat interfaces work. That way, if the current scroll position is at the bottom of the stream, then the auto-scroll will stay active because it's safe to assume the user wants to see the real-time stream. But if the user has moved the scroll position to a previous point in the stream, then the assumption should be that the user wants auto-scroll to be disabled.

For what it's worth, I got caught up by this as well. I'm a bit more accustomed to apps writing back to their configuration file. Typically, they dump out a file with default values and then change values as configured in the GUI/TUI. I'm trying to consistently set up my development environment with Home Manager, so I thought the simplest thing would be to configure OpenCode from within the program and then extract the configuration over to my Home Manager config. In general, I find this approach a lot easier to follow when getting started than trying to compose a config file from a bunch of documentation snippets in an application I've never successfully configured before.

In any event, I spent a fair bit of time trying to figure out where everything was. The docs and, consequently, search engines indicated config would be in a place that it ultimately wasn't being written to. Without a doubt, I assumed the configuration file would be updated and that's not guaranteed behavior, but the assumption was based on how other tools typically work. I was about to dig into the source, but I ultimately worked it out by changing the theme and then grepping on the theme value until I discovered _~/.local/state/opencode_.

@rekram1-node I forgot to mention a more detailed use case centered around this issue. First of all, this bug doesn't really apply to subagent delegations because they are operationally new sessions being spawned each time a subagent is delegated. So, you can safely switch your subagent models mid-session; unless one day OpenCode introduces multi-turn, reusable subagent sessions which I can't imagine why.

My issue comes specifically from the primary session (my Orchestrator) switching models' mid-session.

I did play around with a third-party ChatGPT OAuth plugin before this release and ran into a similar issue except I was able to switch to a ChatGPT model and continue in older sessions that had been started with an API model. Question, are you guys going to support both API and OAuth loaded at the same time within OpenCode? Or is it only either or... I'm at that cusp where it's least expensive for me to pay for API usage vs having a higher-level monthly subscription that gives you the higher limits. But I think I'd rather have a pay-per-month subscription for my "normal" month to month usage and retain the ability to flip over to the API when I hit a limit during those months of heavy project work.
